checker.notes: Statement 24 words, one number (1918), plain words. Facts 9-12 words each, all true, none about tram sales or early withdrawal. Voluntary distancing before official orders is documented for COVID, but no known Budapest 1918 tram-ticket study. Venues real and on topic.

Statement 22 words, no numbers. Facts 12/9/11/9 words, all true and general (repeatability, fixed reference, vibration concern, shift patterns); none asserts that footfall shakes floors. Footfall vibration is a known issue for microscopes and measuring machines, but not a known result for stiff industrial robot arms. Both venues are real Elsevier journals in the field.

issues: Invented finding is a tweak of a known real result: personalised SMS reminders improving childhood vaccination uptake have been trialled in Kenya and elsewhere, so a 'personal text works' claim risks reading as true.
The rewrite drops the original invented element (evening-before vs week-ahead timing) and replaces it with a personalisation angle that sits closer to real literature.

facts.fact: Drew on a fatigue database compiled from around 3,000 published papers
facts.evidence: The database (FatigueData-AM2022) is generated with the help of machine learning and image processing techniques by using around 3000 scientific papers on fatigue or crack propagation of additively manufactured metals

facts.fact: Covered 3D-printed aluminum, steel and titanium parts
facts.evidence: The study focused on additively manufactured aluminium, steel and titanium.

facts.fact: Compared build direction, heat treatment and surface finishing like machining and polishing
facts.evidence: Three manufacturing parameters were considered, namely the manufacturing direction, heat-treatment and surface operations ... The surface operation categories machining, polishing and both machining and polishing were used

facts.fact: Long-life fatigue strength averaged 0.18 to 0.21 of breaking strength, depending on loading
facts.evidence: the mean endurance limit as a ratio to ultimate tensile strength was 0.18 and 0.21 for 0.1 and -1 loading ratios, respectively, without any statistical analysis.

facts.fact: Machine-learning models needed more inputs, like defects, to predict fatigue reliably
facts.evidence: our investigation indicates it is necessary to account for parameters in addition to those considered here such as manufacturing processes, material properties, material microstructure and defects to make reliable fatigue property estimates ... using machine learning.

checker.notes: Paper text is cut off partway through the main effect analysis; the surface-operation and machine-learning conclusions are supported by the abstract, and the key findings' figures (3000 papers, 0/90 degree builds, 59% of k between 3 and 6, 0.18/0.21) all appear in the available text. Endurance limit is defined at 2x10^6 cycles, so 'long-life fatigue strength' and 'breaking strength' (ultimate tensile strength) are fair plain-language renderings.

facts.fact: Compared over 39,000 homes at 770 settlements worldwide
facts.evidence: Over 39,000 individual residential units were coded as having fortifications present or absent ... We compared residential disparity ... at sites around the world (n = 770)

facts.fact: Homes span as far back as 10,000 years ago
facts.evidence: at sites around the world (n = 770) dating as far back as 10,000 y ago.

facts.fact: Wealth gap measured by house-size differences within each settlement
facts.evidence: Our proxy for inequality is residential disparity - the difference between the sizes (m2) of residential units (i.e., housing) within a settlement expressed as a Gini coefficient

facts.fact: In the earliest eras, fortified sites often had equal or smaller gaps
facts.evidence: we also found long periods, especially in the earliest eras represented in the database, when fortified settlements had residential disparity less than or equal to unfortified settlements.

facts.fact: Where land, not labor, limited farming, the bigger gaps lasted much longer
facts.evidence: Ratcheting-up is strong and sustained where land, not people, is the limiting factor in food production but not where people and their labor are the limiting factor.

checker.notes: Some counts in the paper disagree with each other: the database has 53,466 units at 1,176 sites, the figure caption says 'over 35,000' and the Discussion says 'nearly 12k' fortified residences against 13,372 in the abstract. The item uses the abstract's 39,000/770, which the text supports. 'But not where power was shared more' rests on 'Societies coded as less collective tend to have larger residential disparity at fortified settlements' and on the early collective societies; this is acceptable but close to the limit. Fact 5 is the authors' explanation, drawn from two regional case studies (Southwest Asia, long-lived, against Southeast North America, short-lived).

facts.fact: Covered 168 countries; 137 tax road fuel, 31 subsidise it
facts.evidence: The data cover 168 countries across four income levels ... We found that 137 countries implement a net tax on road vehicle fuel, whereas 31 countries provide net subsidies to road vehicle fuel

facts.fact: Fuel taxes raised over 920 billion US dollars in 2023
facts.evidence: In total, we estimated that over US$920 billion (in 2024 US dollars) were collected in fuel tax revenues across the 137 taxing countries in 2023.

facts.fact: Poorest countries average over 9% of revenue from fuel tax; richer ones around 2-4%
facts.evidence: low-income countries are the most affected, with over 9% average exposure, whereas upper-middle- and high-income countries face considerably lower levels, around 2-4% on average.

facts.fact: Tax measured as gap between local pump prices and a world benchmark price
facts.evidence: The difference between the country-specific retail price ... and the global benchmark price ... represents a tax if the local price is higher or a subsidy if lower.

facts.fact: Seven highly exposed countries, including Yemen and Kenya, also face debt crises
facts.evidence: many exposed countries are in a debt crisis ... Consequently, some countries in the upper-left quadrant of Fig. 2—namely, Yemen, Benin, Lebanon, Mozambique, Madagascar, Kenya and Suriname—now face a double exposure

checker.notes: The 920 billion figure is in 2024 US dollars for the 137 taxing countries; the abstract rounds it to about US$900 billion, so both are consistent. The seven countries are named as examples ('some countries'), not as an exhaustive list; the fact's wording does not claim exclusivity. The paper frames exposure as potential future revenue loss; 'puts their budgets most at risk' matches that framing. All key-finding numbers (4-8%, r = -0.27 for 115 countries, US$735 billion, about three times) appear in the text.

facts.evidence: representing 4.78% of the 2013 and 20.90% of the 2022 landslide area. These recurrent failures provide a critical basis for evaluating how inherited damage... governed hillslope response

checker.notes: Statement is exactly 28 words (the limit) with one number ('nine'). The paper text is cut off just before the 20.90% sentence, but 'These recurrent failures' makes clear that it means overlapping failures. Do not mix it up with the separate equal-shaking figure (0.93 km2, 20.82%), which the key findings report correctly. The text carries no cross-event accuracy numbers, so 'predicted well' should stay qualitative, as it does. The key finding saying slopes 'had not fully relaxed nearly a decade after 2013' comes from the Discussion, not the Results section it is attributed to, but its content is accurate.
